title: Design reactive diff and event engine
description: Design the engine that turns repeated materialized session observations into a structured stream of inserts, updates, deletes, and derived session changes.
design: At worst, watch DB/WAL file changes, re-query known scopes, materialize into a store, and diff against the previous store. Prefer an event cursor if opencode's event tables are reliable. Output should be useful to downstream consumers and not leak backend implementation details.
acceptance_criteria:
- Event envelope includes cursor/revision, entity key, operation, timestamps, and raw/typed payload references.
- Engine can compare two materialized stores or one incoming observation against a store.
- Design covers update coalescing, ordering, deletions, partial failures, and backpressure.
- Relationship to futures-signals streams/signals is documented.

title: Spike Turso/libSQL source backend
description: Add or design a Turso/libSQL-backed source layer for reading opencode SQLite-compatible state from Rust.
design: Evaluate `turso`/libSQL Rust APIs for local SQLite interoperation, read-only snapshots, prepared queries, JSON payload reads, and compatibility with opencode's DB/WAL setup. Compare against rusqlite only as a baseline.
acceptance_criteria:
- Minimal Turso/libSQL read path can list projects, sessions, messages, and parts from a copied fixture DB or live-safe snapshot.
- Connection and transaction semantics are documented.
- Compatibility gaps with opencode SQLite/WAL are recorded.
- Source backend fits the materialized store/diff design.
notes: Spike committed. Remaining: WAL stress test, snapshot consistency bounds, connect to materialized store trait.

title: Investigate opencode SQLite WAL and follow strategies
description: Determine how opencode opens SQLite, whether WAL is enabled, what files change during live sessions, and which follow strategy can produce reliable change streams.
design: Explore live DB pragmas, WAL behavior, update timestamps, event/event_sequence tables, session_entry, and file watching behavior. Compare polling `time_updated`, watching DB/WAL files, event table cursors, and opencode API/server event sources.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document current journal mode and WAL-related files.
- Identify which tables change for new user prompts, assistant responses, tool calls, and question answers.
- Compare follow strategies with correctness and latency tradeoffs.
- Recommend first implementation target for reactive diffing.

title: Design materialized session store trait
description: Define a trait for storing materialized session state so diffing can compare incoming state against memory-backed or SQL-backed stores using the same interface.
design: The trait should model session/message/part/session_entry identity, revisions, ordering, raw payload preservation, and typed projections. Backends should include in-memory and Turso/SQLite. Diffing should be expressed as comparing two store views, not as a special case of one live DB.
acceptance_criteria:
- Trait contract documents identity keys, ordering keys, revision/version semantics, and payload fidelity.
- In-memory and SQL-backed backend responsibilities are clear.
- Diff engine can consume two store views without knowing backend details.
- Contract covers partial hydration and raw JSON preservation.

title: Capture opencode SQLite schema as first-class design artifact
description: Record the current opencode SQLite table schema, row JSON payload assumptions, indexes, and known migration state in this repository so redesign discussions have a shared source of truth.
design: Use a checked-in document or fixture-derived schema artifact that excludes secrets and account tokens. Include tables relevant to sessions, messages, parts, events, todos, workspaces, and shares. Treat account/control_account tables as sensitive and document structure only if needed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repository contains a schema artifact derived from current opencode SQLite storage.
- Artifact excludes row data that may contain account tokens or secrets.
- `doc/genesis-sqlite.md` links to or embeds the schema summary.
- Schema artifact identifies unknowns and follow-up questions around WAL, event tables, and session_entry semantics.

title: Evaluate futures-signals for materialized session streams
description: Assess how `futures-signals` can represent live opencode session materialization, diffs, and downstream reactive views in Rust.
design: Map session collections, message lists, part lists, and derived views to signal/stream primitives. Determine where plain futures streams are enough and where signals add value. Include ergonomics for consumers like exp2span.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document candidate signal/stream types for sessions, messages, parts, and event streams.
- Identify integration points with the diff engine.
- Note constraints around async runtimes, Send/Sync, and backpressure.
- Provide recommendation for first reactive API surface.

title: Read opencode state from Btrfs snapshots
description: Implement or design reader support for opening opencode SQLite state from Btrfs snapshots instead of live mutable directories.
design: Build on snapshot capture. Reader should accept a snapshot root and resolve opencode DB/WAL paths from that root. It should make fixture generation and diff testing reproducible without racing live writes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reader can target a snapshot root instead of the live XDG data root.
- Snapshot reads include SQLite DB, WAL, and SHM consistency considerations.
- Tests or documented procedure show reading a session from a snapshot.
- Failure modes for missing or stale snapshot files are explicit.

title: Design Btrfs snapshot capture for opencode state directories
description: Define how to create safe point-in-time Btrfs snapshots of opencode state directories before reading or testing against live SQLite/WAL files.
design: Snapshot scope should include `~/.local/share/opencode` and any WAL/SHM files needed for a consistent read. The design should cover naming, retention, permissions, privacy, and whether snapshots are test-only or part of production workflows.
acceptance_criteria:
- Snapshot scope and consistency model are documented.
- Design identifies commands/APIs needed to create and clean snapshots.
- Risks around WAL, secrets, disk usage, and permissions are documented.
- Follow-up implementation tickets can build from the design.

title: Build session fixture/builder API
description: Create a nice builder for constructing sessions, messages, parts, session entries, todos, and other relevant entities for tests and examples.
design: Builder should target the modern SQLite/Turso data model rather than the legacy file-tree format. It should support constructing materialized stores and emitting SQLite-compatible rows or in-memory store records.
acceptance_criteria:
- Builder can construct a session with messages and parts.
- Builder can add tool, text, reasoning, step-start, and step-finish records.
- Builder can emit records into the materialized store trait or a test SQLite/Turso database.
- API keeps raw JSON and typed helper paths available for tests.

title: Add bon::Builder to StoragePaths
description:
Replace manual struct assembly with builder pattern for safer path configuration.

Current state (`src/storage/paths.rs:5-13`):
- 7 related fields that must stay consistent
- `detect()` and `from_base()` constructors
- Test in `src/storage/paths.rs:141` uses literal struct assembly

Target:
```rust
let paths = StoragePaths::builder()
    .base(path_buf)
    .build()?;

// Or for tests:
let paths = StoragePaths::builder()
    .root("/test/storage")
    .session("/test/storage/session")
    .message("/test/storage/message")
    .part("/test/storage/part")
    .diff("/test/storage/session_diff")
    .snapshot("/test/storage/snapshot")
    .migration("/test/storage/migration")
    .build();
```

Acceptance:
- `StoragePaths` derives `bon::Builder`
- `detect()` and `from_base()` remain as convenience methods
- Test updated to use builder

title: Add bon::Builder to SessionMaterializer
description:
Replace `new()`, `detect()`, `with_paths()`, `with_reader()` constructors with a unified builder pattern.

Current API (`src/materializer.rs:16-33`):
- `SessionMaterializer::new()` - auto-detect paths
- `SessionMaterializer::detect()` - same as new
- `SessionMaterializer::with_paths(StoragePaths)` - explicit paths
- `SessionMaterializer::with_reader(FileReader)` - custom reader

Target API:
```rust
let m = SessionMaterializer::builder()
    .paths(storage_paths)  // or .detect_paths() or .reader(file_reader)
    .build()?;
```

Acceptance:
- `SessionMaterializer` derives `bon::Builder`
- Existing constructors deprecated or removed
- `SessionLoader` similarly updated for consistency
- Tests pass

title: Investigate Feldera DBSP for session diff dataflow
description: Explore whether Feldera/DBSP is a good fit for incremental opencode session materialization, diffing, and derived analytics.
design: Compare hand-rolled store diffing against DBSP-style incremental dataflow. Look at experiments in `~/src/tiamux` and planned `~/src/nirimat` for local patterns. Focus on whether DBSP helps with derived views, not just novelty.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document candidate DBSP inputs, collections, and derived outputs.
- Identify where DBSP reduces complexity versus adds overhead.
- Note integration risks for library consumers.
- Recommend whether to spike, defer, or avoid DBSP in the first rebuild.

acceptance_criteria:

- doc/qa-struct.md includes key decisions to reevaluate

title: Add bon::Builder to large serde domain structs
description:
Add builders to message/part domain types with many optional fields to simplify test fixtures and future synthetic data generation.

Candidates:
- `AssistantMessage` (`src/types/message.rs:63-88`) - 15 fields, many optional
- `UserMessage` (`src/types/message.rs:30-45`) - 9 fields, many optional
- `ToolStateCompleted` (`src/types/part.rs:128-137`) - 6 fields
- `SubtaskPart` (`src/types/part.rs:254-264`) - 7 fields

These are serde types, so builder is primarily for programmatic construction (tests, fixtures).

Acceptance:
- Selected structs derive `bon::Builder`
- At least one test demonstrates cleaner fixture construction
- Serde behavior unchanged

title: Add bon::Builder to index metadata structs

Add builders to `SessionMeta`, `MessageMeta`, and `PartRef` to improve hot-path construction clarity.

Locations:
- `SessionMeta` literal at `src/index.rs:295-305`
- `MessageMeta` literal at `src/index.rs:335-343`

Target:

SessionMeta::builder()
    .id(session_id.clone())
    .title(session.title)

title: Introduce bon::Builder across key types
description:
Replace manual constructor patterns with `bon::Builder` derive to reduce API surface, improve ergonomics, and make future configuration options additive without proliferating `with_*` variants.

Key goals:
- Unify mutually exclusive construction modes into fluent builder APIs
- Reduce invalid state combinations for structs with many related fields
- Make test fixtures and synthetic data creation cleaner
- Establish a consistent pattern for configuration-heavy types
notes: Assessment (2026-05-29): this epic and all children target the old file-per-entity API surface (StoragePaths, SessionMaterializer, index metadata structs, domain structs). Those modules are now marked deprecated. This epic needs rescoping to the SQLite/Turso data model before any children can proceed. The bon::Builder pattern itself is still desired, but the target types will change.

title: Optimize update-read path to index only newly appended content
description: Investigate what content is typically appended in update operations and optimize the indexing to only process newly appended content rather than re-indexing entire files/structures.
notes: Assessment (2026-05-29): this ticket was filed during the file-per-entity JSON storage era. opencode has since moved to SQLite storage, making the original framing obsolete. Should be closed or re-scoped to SQLite append/change detection semantics if the optimization question is still relevant.
